about: How an account's <h> is derived from its subject (6j6v.dbmd, consumer contract v2.1, runbook step A3 (ii)): the first 32 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of "<issuer>:<sub>". The issuer is taken byte for byte, never normalised: a trailing slash is a different issuer and a different <h>. The two nxsflow vectors were confirmed by nexflowit (nexflowit-app main 0bb5dee, MemberIdentity.userId) and recomputed by nexus. nxs_fold_ddb::deny::AccountHash::of_subject is pinned to this file by its unit tests.

cases.why: the staging issuer, confirmed by nexflowit
the production issuer, confirmed by nexflowit
a trailing slash on the issuer is not normalised away: a different <h> than the production issuer's
